subject: Game Theory
title: OPEC's Dilemma
description: A fast breakdown of OPEC's Dilemma for builders.

hook.text: OPEC controls 40% of global oil. Its members agree on production quotas. Few actually follow them.

buildup.text: Each member benefits from secretly pumping extra barrels. More oil means more revenue—for the cheater.

discovery.text: Saudi Arabia often plays enforcer, cutting its own production to offset others' cheating.

twist.text: In 2020, Saudi Arabia flooded the market to punish Russia for refusing cuts, crashing oil to $20 a barrel.

climax.text: OPEC survives because members need each other, but it limps along—perpetually undermined by defection.

quiz.question: Why does Saudi Arabia sometimes flood the oil market?
options: To punish other producers who refuse to cut output
